cells.tense: The direction is here now, and your hands are already in it.
cells.act: tell the truth with care for when and how
cells.ask: In one conversation that matters, say the true thing plainly and then stop. No cushioning, no softer second version. Let the moment you pick do half the work.
cells.core:
The pull toward what you care about has gotten into the ordinary days. You can tell a step that's really yours from one you took because it was expected, and you take fewer of the second kind now. That light isn't somewhere you visit; it's the thing you steer by, and the steering shows up in small choices most people wouldn't notice.

The place it goes crooked is timing with people. You know what's true, and you say it in a form the other person can hold — that's the whole skill, and you have it. Try it once this week: one true sentence, no cushioning after. The truth lands cleaner without the padding than you expect, and the person stays.
cells.sheetLine: You know which way is yours, and lately your feet agree.
cells.verb: move what you care about into the open where it can reach someone
cells.place: the stretch of water where the far light you've been steering by first shows itself

cells.tense: The light has gotten out ahead of your feet, and you're still talking about it.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Pick one inch of the thing you keep describing and move it — one call, one page, one real step. Not the plan, just the inch, done slowly and not taken back. No deadline attached.
cells.core:
When the pull is going into your hands, the days feel pointed and you take the step while it's small. Overheated, the far version arrives first. You've already pictured the room full, the meaning landed, the people changed, and the step at your feet reads as an insult to that picture. So the picture grows and the actual inch gets skipped. The pull is real and sound. It has outrun your hands, and you feel the lag as pressure.

Come back through the ground. One inch moved for real, and not undone, settles more than another bright plan. You'll know which one you did by how you feel at dinner: the picture drains you, the inch doesn't.

cells.tense: The light was there once, and you've been standing past it since.
cells.act: think it through to its sharp point
cells.ask: Take a thought you keep circling and stop at its sharp point — the last line, the clean end of it. You don't have to go further. Just find where the point is and leave it there.
cells.core:
What you care about still pulls at you, but it's behind you now — a door you passed and didn't go through — and you've been explaining the hallway ever since. Pleasure in the work comes through muted. You still care. You've stopped letting the caring aim anywhere, because aiming means moving.

Charge a different nerve first: the clean one. Reasoning something to its sharp point is easy for you and costs almost nothing. Take one circling thought to its actual end and get it onto paper. That small act of clarity is what gets current back through the starved part. You don't have to feel your way out of this.

cells.tense: The pull is moving people, and you're calling it something smaller.
cells.act: hold the clarity steady and tempered
cells.ask: When what you make with someone gets called a hobby or a phase, don't agree and don't argue. Keep the truer name quietly and carry on — a practice, nothing to defend.
cells.core:
You move people through what you care about, and that's real — they catch the direction off you before you've said anything about it. Then someone asks what it's for, and your own words come out smaller than the thing: a side interest, a way to pass time, nothing serious. The work is doing its job. What you're calling it is what's off.

You don't have to build a case. When the small name comes, don't agree and don't fight — just keep the truer one quietly and go on. What you make with people around this counts as what it is.
